paper.title: Reward Maximization for Pure Exploration: Minimax Optimal Good Arm Identification for Nonparametric Multi-Armed Bandits

settings.name_in_paper: Good arm identification / threshold identification (fixed confidence) for nonparametric bounded bandits

parameters.restriction: conditional arm means E[X_t|A_t=a,F_{t-1}] = mu_a constant over time

unmapped: Reward distributions are nonparametric on [0,1] and may change over time exogenously or endogenously (depending on history), only the conditional mean of each arm given the past is fixed (no exact environment term; mapped to adversarial_restricted)
Learner knows the threshold xi; goal is to label arms as above/below xi with delta-level error control and minimize stopping times tau_{G,i} (i-th good arm) and tau_stop
settings.definition_quote:
Beyond boundedness, we assume that when conditioned on 


any possible previous observations $\Fcal_{t-1}$ and any action $A_t$ at time $t$, the conditional arm means $\bm\mu\equiv\{\mu_1, ..., \mu_K\}\in[0,1]^K$ remain constant:
$$
\forall t \in \NN, \ \forall a \in[K],

\ \ \EE[X_t|A_t=a, \Fcal_{t-1}] = \mu_a. 
$$
Let $\Pcal(\mu_a)$ be the set of all \emph{distributional sequences} on $[0,1]^\infty$ such that $\EE[X_t| A_t=a, \Fcal_{t-1}] = \mu_a$.

settings.name_in_paper: Anytime-valid one-sided mean test for a single arm (e-power)

parameters.restriction: conditional arm mean fixed over time

unmapped: Objective is the e-power (expected log-growth per pull) of an anytime-valid e-process testing H^-_a: mu_a <= xi or H^+_a: mu_a > xi, under the worst-case distributional sequence with conditional mean mu_a
settings.definition_quote: For an $e$-process $E = (E_t)_{t \in \NN}$ with respect to null hypothesis set $\Hcal$, we define $e$-power of any  $P \not\in \Hcal$ as $\EE_{P}[\log(E_t)]/t$.
